 Rutgers Men’s Basketball Heads West For 2026 Players Era Festival
 Scarlet Knights to get first real test of 2026-2027 season.
 by Andrew Rice Nov 16, 2026, 8:46 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 After defeating Bryant 72-51 and sweeping their early non-conference slate, Rutgers men’s basketball will head west to play in the Players Era Festival. This will be their first real test of the season, as they will compete in the eight team bracket and be matched up against No.8 Houston on Tuesday, either No.1 Florida or Notre Dame on Wednesday, and another quality opponent on Thursday, depending on the result of the first two games.
 Houston will likely be one of the toughest opponents the Knights will have to play all season. The Cougars have thrashed their three opponents so far this season, defeating both Jax State and La Sallee by a combined score of 95 points and defeating Cal 86-68. They are led offensively by Dedan Thomas Jr., who is averaging 17.7 points per game. He also leads his team in assists per game with 6.7. Delrecco Gillespie leads the Cougars in rebounds with 6.3 per game. Houston is rated as the No.3 team according to KenPom, while Rutgers is the No. 74 team. The Knights have also played the second-weakest schedule in the country so far this season, according to KenPom, with Houston’s out-of-conference schedule floating in the lower 200s so far.
 Next for the Knights will either be Florida or Notre Dame, depending on the results of the first game. Florida is the No.1 team in the nation on KenPom and in the AP Poll, while Notre Dame comes in at No. 68. The Gators have already pulled off power conference wins over teams like Miami and Florida State, while Notre Dame has done the same by beating Villanova in a game that was played in Italy. The Gators are led by Thomas Haugh, a Second Team All-American last season who is averaging 17.1 points per game, while the Fighting Irish are led by Ethan Roberts, who is averaging 19.8 points per game.
 Rutgers third opponent will be dependent on the results of the first two games, with Kansas, UNLV, West Virginia or Auburn being a possible matchup for Rutgers.
 Rutgers tournament performance will tell fans a lot about the new-look Knights in the coming days. While the games against Houston and (possibly) Florida will be extremely tough sledding, if Rutgers can take care of Notre Dame and their game 3 opponent, it will be an improvement compared to the two previous years.
 Rutgers opens the tournament on Tuesday against Houston at 2 p.m. ET at Michelob ULTRA Arena. Live coverage for the game will be available on ESPN. On Wednesday, the Knights will face Florida or Notre Dame. A win over Houston would send Rutgers to the semifinals at 4:30 p.m.; a loss would send them to the first consolation game at 2 p.m. Thursday’s opponent will come from the bottom half of the bracket: Kansas, UNLV, West Virginia, or Auburn. Times for Thursday’s games are yet to be determined.
